property_summary: After calling setOwner(alice) by the original owner, the reference sets owner to alice while the bug sets owner to address(0); the assertion checks that owner equals alice.
After setOwner is called by the owner, the reference updates owner to the new address, while the buggy version leaves owner unchanged.
Call setOwner(alice) as bob, the reference sets owner to alice, the bug sets owner to msg.sender (bob).
After a single call to setOwner(alice), the reference sets owner to alice, while the bug sets owner to msg.sender, so reading c.owner() after that call detects the divergence.

After calling setOwner(msg.sender) as the owner, the reference keeps owner unchanged, while the bug sets owner to msg.sender again (no change), but if a different address calls setOwner(alice), the reference sets owner to alice while the bug sets owner to that caller's address, and reading c.owner() after two calls reveals the divergence.
After calling setOwner(alice) as the owner (address(this)), the reference sets owner to alice; the bug sets owner to address(this); reading c.owner() after the call reveals the divergence.

When non-owner calls setOwner(address), the reference contract sets owner (require(msg.sender == owner) passes because msg.sender is owner in that scenario?), but the mutant always reverts (require(false)), so after a call by a non-owner, the reference would revert and not change owner, while the mutant also reverts — wait, need to pick a scenario where they differ. Actually, for the reference, onlyOwner checks msg.sender == owner; for the mutant, it always reverts. So a call from owner will succeed in reference and fail in mutant. Concrete: owner calls setOwner(newOwner). After call, reference has new owner, mutant owner unchanged (since revert).
After a call to setOwner by a non-owner address, the reference reverts (owner unchanged) while the buggy version sets owner to the non-owner address.
After calling setOwner(address) as owner, P returns true while M returns false, checked by storing the return value in a boolean.
After calling setOwner with the owner address itself, the reference contract keeps owner unchanged, but the buggy contract sets owner to a fixed dummy address, so reading owner afterwards differs.
